text.tspan: One thing I'll tell you so that you appreciate this result. Remember how we found that the
Fisher information of a single receptor was equal to the rate of turning on and off?
That is, the inverse of the average duration of an ON/OFF cycle. In our model, we choose
our diffusion coefficient D, which sets the timescale of the polymer simulation, such that
the closing and opening times of a polymer were much larger than the burst time of a single
receptor. Still, comparing the Fisher information rates in the same units, we found that the
polymer can still give you more sensitivity, per unit time, than a single receptor. This is
true even if it takes the polymer over 100 times longer to produce a single "burst"
